newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds surge after Sept jobs report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds surge after Sept jobs report.

text.p: A weaker-than-expected jobs report set U.S. mortgage-backed securities trading higher and generally holding their ground against Treasuries on Friday, traders and fixed-income analysts said.
"The mortgage market has been very good given the sharp rise and perhaps some change in sentiment," said Bill Powers, managing director and and mortgage-backed specialist at PIMCO.

Although higher coupons often lag discounts in a bull market, premiums performed well on Friday. Some players may have been "caught with less duration that they wanted" and tried to "catch up" by buying premium products, Powers said.

Additionally, lack of selling by mortgage bankers throughout the week may have helped pass-throughs keep pace with Treasuries, he said. "That may change if mortgage bankers start selling early next week, Powers added.
Traders said buying was spotty on Friday, but they mentioned agency purchasing of 7.5- and 7.0-percent pass-throughs.
By late Friday, pass-throughs ranged from 5/32 to 24/32 higher. Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent coupons were up 19/32 at 99-31/32, yielding 110 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
The 10-year Treasury note, was up 30/32 to yield 6.47 percent.
On Friday morning, the Labor Department said non-farm payrolls fell 40,000 in September after a rise of 241,000 in August. Wall Street economist in a Reuters poll had forecast an increase of 166,000.

"It's an indication the underlying weakness in the economy is hitting the labor market and the (Federal Reserve) is vindicated in not raising rates," Lacy Hunt, chief economist at HSBC Markets Inc, said of the report.
